<output>
# dua (Disk Usage Analyzer)

**dua** is a tool to conveniently learn about the usage of disk space of a given directory. It's parallel by default and will max out your SSD, providing relevant information as fast as possible. Optionally delete superfluous data, and do so more quickly than `rm`.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/kDnXUOeqBxZVMoWuFNqzfpeey)

## Installation

### Binary Release 

#### MacOS

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### MacOS via [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org):
```sh
sudo port selfupdate
sudo port install dua-cli
```

#### MacOS via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)
```sh
brew update
brew install dua-cli
```

#### Linux

Linux requires the target to be specified explicitly to obtain the MUSL build.

```sh
curl -LSfs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Byron/dua-cli/master/ci/install.sh | \
    sh -s -- --git Byron/dua-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --crate dua --tag v2.29.0
```

#### Windows via [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/)
```sh
scoop install dua
```

#### Windows via [WinGet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/package-manager/winget/)
```sh
winget install Byron.dua-cli
```

#### Pre-built Binaries

See the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases) for manual installation of a binary, pre-built for many platforms.

#### VoidLinux
Via `xbps` on your VoidLinux system.

```
xbps-install dua-cli
```

#### Fedora
Via `dnf` on your Fedora system.

```
sudo dnf install dua-cli
```

#### Arch Linux
Via `pacman` on your ArchLinux system.

```
sudo pacman -S dua-cli
```

#### NixOS
https://search.nixos.org/packages?channel=23.11&show=dua&from=0&size=50&sort=relevance&type=packages&query=dua

Nix-shell (temporary)

```
nix-shell -p dua
```

NixOS configuration

```
  environment.systemPackages = [
    pkgs.dua
  ];
```

#### NetBSD
Via `pkgin` on your NetBSD system.

```
pkgin install dua-cli
```

Or, building from source

```
cd /usr/pkgsrc/sysutils/dua-cli
make install
```

#### Windows

You will find pre-built binaries for Windows in the [releases section](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/releases).

#### x-cmd

[x-cmd](https://www.x-cmd.com/) is a **toolbox for Posix Shell**, offering a lightweight package manager built using shell and awk.
```sh
x env use dua
```
- Additionally, the [`x dua ...`](https://www.x-cmd.com/pkg/dua#dua) command is available, which automatically installs `dua` without affecting the environment, such as not modifying the `PATH` variable.

## Usage

```bash
# count the space used in the current working directory
dua
# count the space used in all directories that are not hidden
dua *
# learn about additional functionality
dua aggregate --help
```

### Interactive Mode

Launch into interactive mode with the `i` or `interactive` subcommand. Get help on keyboard
shortcuts with `?`.
Use this mode to explore, and/or to delete files and directories to release disk space.

Please note that great care has been taken to prevent accidental deletions due to a multi-stage
process, which makes this mode viable for exploration.

```bash
dua i
dua interactive
```

## Limitations

* Does not show symbolic links at all if no path is provided when invoking `dua`
  * in an effort to skip symbolic links, for now there are pruned and are not used as a root. Symbolic links will be shown if they
    are not a traversal root, but will not be followed.
* Interactive mode only looks good in dark terminals (see [this issue](https://github.com/Byron/dua-cli/issues/13))
* File names in main window are not truncated if too large. They are cut off on the right.
* There are plenty of examples in test fixtures which don't render correctly in interactive mode.
  This can be due to graphemes not interpreted correctly. With Chinese characters for instance,
  column sizes are not correctly computed, leading to certain columns not being shown.
  In other cases, the terminal gets things wrong - I use alacritty, and with certain characters it
  performs worse than, say iTerm3.
* In interactive mode, you will need about 60MB of memory for 1 million entries in the graph.
* In interactive mode, the maximum amount of files is limited to 2^32 - 1 entries.

## Similar Programs 

* **CLI:**
  * `du`
  * [`dust`](https://github.com/bootandy/dust)
  * [`dutree`](https://github.com/nachoparker/dutree)
  * [`pdu`](https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage)
* **TUI:**
  * [`ncdu`](https://dev.yorhel.nl/ncdu)
  * [`gdu`](https://github.com/dundee/gdu)
  * [`godu`](https://github.com/viktomas/godu)
* **GUI:**
  * [GNOME's Disk Usage Analyzer, a.k.a. `baobab`](https://wiki.gnome.org/action/show/Apps/DiskUsageAnalyzer)
  * [Filelight](https://apps.kde.org/filelight/)

import subprocess, time, sys, os

cmd = sys.argv[4:]
subprocess.run(['tmux','kill-session','-t',sess], stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
subprocess.run(['tmux','new-session','-d','-s',sess,'-x',str(cols),'-y',str(rows)]+cmd)
time.sleep(1.2)
i=0
while True:
    line = sys.stdin.readline()
    if not line: break
    line=line.strip()
    if line.startswith('k:'):
        keys = line[2:]
        tm = ['tmux','send-keys','-t',sess]
        if keys:
            for k in keys.split(','):
                tm.append('-K' if k.startswith('C-') or k.startswith('Esc') or k.startswith('BSpace') or k.startswith('PgUp') or k.startswith('PgDn') or k.startswith('Home') or k.startswith('End') or k.startswith('Space') or k.startswith('Enter') else '-l')
                tm.append(k)

        print('=== CAPTURE %d after %s'%(i,line[2:]))
        sys.stdout.write(r.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace'))
        sys.stdout.flush()

        time.sleep(float(line[2:]))

        break
    i+=1

PYEOF

cd /tmp && for n in $(seq 6 25) 28 29 31 33 35 37 40 45 50 53 100; do if [ ! -d n$n ]; then mkdir n$n; for i in $(seq 1 $n); do head -c 10 /dev/zero > n$n/f$i; done; fi; done; for n in $(seq 6 25) 28 29 31 33 35 37 40 45 50 53 100; do tmux kill-session -t c 2>/dev/null; tmux new-session -d -s c -x 100 -y 30 "/workspace/executable i /tmp/n$n"; sleep 1.6; tmux capture-pane -t c -p > /tmp/cx.txt; python3 -c "
lines=open('/tmp/cx.txt').read().split('\n')
bs=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.endswith('\u2588')]
ss=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.endswith('\u2551')]
import math
n=$n; H=26; hyp=round(H*H/(H+n-1))
print('n=%3d block=%3d dbl=%3d hyp=%3d %s'%(n,len(bs),len(ss),hyp,'OK' if len(bs)==hyp else 'MISMATCH'))
"; done

actions.command:
cd /tmp && for n in 5 20 60; do for h in 14 20 40; do tmux kill-session -t c 2>/dev/null; tmux new-session -d -s c -x 100 -y $h "/workspace/executable i /tmp/n$n"; sleep 1.6; tmux capture-pane -t c -p > /tmp/cx.txt; python3 -c "
lines=open('/tmp/cx.txt').read().split('\n')
bs=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.endswith('\u2588')]
ss=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.endswith('\u2551')]
n=$n; H=$h-4; hyp=round(H*H/(H+n-1))
print('n=%3d H=%2d block=%3d dbl=%3d hyp=%3d %s'%(n,H,len(bs),len(ss),hyp,'OK' if len(bs)==hyp else 'MISMATCH'))
"; done; done

import sys,re
txt=sys.stdin.read()

    lines=[re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',x) for x in body.split('\n')]
    print('---', ch.split('\n',1)[0])
    for l in lines[2:6]:
        print(repr(l[:120]))
        ps=[j for j,c in enumerate(l) if c=='|']
        print('   pipes at', ps[:5])
"

import subprocess, time, sys, json

    subprocess.run(['tmux','send-keys','-t','b','-l','j'])
    time.sleep(0.45)

    r=subprocess.run(['tmux','capture-pane','-t','b','-p','-e'],capture_output=True)

    sel=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if '\x1b[7m' in l]

    subprocess.run(['tmux','send-keys','-t','b','-l','j'])

import subprocess, time, sys
n=int(sys.argv[1]); H=int(sys.argv[2]); keys=sys.argv[3].split(',') if len(sys.argv)>3 else []

import os, pty, sys, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, json, re
def run(cmd, cols, rows, keys, outfile, settle=3.0, post=1.0):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.environ['TERM']='xterm-256color'
        os.execvp(cmd[0], cmd)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0))
    out = bytearray()
    def drain(t=0.4):
        end = time.time()+t
        while time.time() < end:
            r,_,_ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.05)
            if r:
                try: d = os.read(fd, 65536)
                except OSError: return False
                if not d: return False
                out.extend(d)
                end = time.time()+t
        return True
    drain(settle)
    for k in keys:
        out.extend(('<<KEY:%s>>'%k).encode())
        os.write(fd, k.encode() if isinstance(k,str) else k)
        if not drain(post): break
    try: os.close(fd)
    except OSError: pass
    try: os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
    except ChildProcessError: pass
    open(outfile,'wb').write(bytes(out))

import os, pty, sys, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, json, re
def run(cmd, cols, rows, keys, outfile, settle=3.0, post=1.0):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.environ['TERM']='xterm-256color'
        os.execvp(cmd[0], cmd)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0))
    out = bytearray()
    def drain(t=0.4):
        end = time.time()+t
        while time.time() < end:
            r,_,_ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.05)
            if r:
                try: d = os.read(fd, 65536)
                except OSError: return False
                if not d: return False
                out.extend(d)
                end = time.time()+t
        return True
    drain(settle)
    for k in keys:
        out.extend(('<<KEY:%s>>'%k).encode())
        os.write(fd, k.encode() if isinstance(k,str) else k)
        if not drain(post): break
    try: os.close(fd)
    except OSError: pass
    try: os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
    except ChildProcessError: pass
    open(outfile,'wb').write(bytes(out))

    print('  status:', repr(lines[29]))

def cap(args, cols=200, rows=60, stdin_tty=True):

            except OSError: break
            if not d: break
            out+=d

    let nthreads = nthreads.clamp(1, 1024);

                let mut g = sh.lock().unwrap();
                if g.queue.is_empty() {
                    None
                } else {
                    let t = g.queue.remove(0);
                    g.busy += 1;
                    Some(t)
                }
                    None => None,

                    let mut g = sh.lock().unwrap();
                    g.busy -= 1;
                }
                None => {
                    let busy = {

                        g.busy
                    };
                    if busy == 0 {
                        break;
                    }
                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_micros(200));
                }
            }
        }));

        let _ = h.join();
    }

#!/bin/bash
# compare interactive screens between original and reimplementation
PASS=0; FAIL=0
run() {
  local dir="$1"; local keys="$2"; local w="$3"; local h="$4"
  for which in orig mine; do
    tmux kill-server >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 0.4
    if [ "$which" = "orig" ]; then CMD=/workspace/executable; else CMD=/tmp/executable; fi
    tmux new-session -d -s b -x "$w" -y "$h" -- "$CMD" i "$dir"
    sleep 1.6
    if [ -n "$keys" ]; then
      IFS=','; for k in $keys; do tmux send-keys -t b -l "$k"; sleep 0.6; done; unset IFS
    fi
    sleep 0.8
    tmux capture-pane -t b -p -e > /tmp/tui.$which 2>/dev/null
  done
  if diff -q /tmp/tui.orig /tmp/tui.mine >/dev/null; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "=== DIFF dir=$dir keys=$keys ${w}x${h}"; diff /tmp/tui.orig /tmp/tui.mine | head -12; fi
}
run /tmp/it "" 100 30

run /tmp/it "j,j,j" 100 30
run /tmp/it "s" 100 30

            let a = args[i].clone();

                ctx.end_of_opts = true;
                continue;

                    None => continue,
                }

                match self.short_opt(&a, &mut ctx, args, &mut i) {
                    Some(act) => return act,
                    None => continue,

                if let Some(sub) = lookup_sub(&a) {
                    ctx.sub = sub;
                    ctx.positionals += 1;
                    continue;
                }

                }

            ctx.positionals += 1;
            match ctx.sub {

import os,pty,time,select,fcntl,termios,struct,sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from screen import parse, dump
pid,fd = pty.fork()
if pid==0:
    os.environ['TERM']='xterm-256color'
    os.execvp('/tmp/executable',['dua','i','/tmp/it'])
fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH',30,100,0,0))
out=b''
t=time.time()
while time.time()-t<2.5:
    r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.2)
    if r:
        try: d=os.read(fd,65536)
        except OSError: break
        if not d: break
        out+=d
s=parse(out,100,30)
print(dump(s,7))
os.close(fd)
PYEOF"}
